description: Extends westbound left-turn lane at Clarence Avenue by 12 meters.
BRT includes advanced traffic signal technologies.
College Drive vehicle travel times increase by three minutes.
Improves safety for transit users, pedestrians, cyclists.

chips.text: Councillor Dunner moved to study adaptive signal control technology for College Drive BRT.
Emergency responders could use preemption technology for faster response times.
Councillors pushed for advanced adaptive signal control technology for initial BRT launch.
College Drive BRT could be Saskatoon's first pilot for adaptive signal control technology.
Cost of adaptive signal control technology for initial launch remains unknown.
Administration will report back on adaptive signal control technology options and costs.

segments.title: Staff Presentation on Corridor Improvements
segments.takeaway: Administration presented an information report detailing advanced traffic management technology and left-turn storage capacity for the College Drive Link Corridor.

segments.title: Committee Questions on Corridor Details
segments.takeaway: Committee members questioned staff on transit and vehicle travel times, specific technologies, emergency vehicle preemption costs, and left-turn lane modifications.

segments.title: Motion for Adaptive Signal Control Technology Report
segments.takeaway: Committee passed a motion requesting administration to report back on including adaptive signal control technology in the BRT launch, including costs and funding opportunities.

description: City to explore horse-drawn carriage business licensing options.
Administration will report on framework for unique business requests.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer apologized for significant delays in processing the business license application.
Rich Pilon, owner of Saskatoon Sleigh Rides, is seeking a business license.
Administration committed to a fast report on licensing options and considering a temporary permit.

segments.title: Applicant's Presentation
segments.takeaway: Jackie Pilon, representing Rich Pilon, requested a business license for Saskatoon Sleigh Rides, highlighting delays and existing traffic bylaw provisions for horse-drawn carriages.

segments.title: Administration's Initial Comments
segments.takeaway: Administration stated there's no existing policy or bylaw to support such a business license and apologized for delays, noting a need for governance improvements for unique inquiries.

segments.title: Questions for the Applicant
segments.takeaway: Councillors questioned the discrepancy in application dates and the historical operation of horse-drawn carriages without a formal business license.

segments.title: Questions for Administration
segments.takeaway: Councillors pressed administration on the lack of a framework for such businesses, the historical operation of similar services, and the process for resolving the application.

segments.title: Motion for Report Back
segments.takeaway: Councillor Donauer moved that administration report back expeditiously with options for business licensing for horse-drawn carriage services and a framework for one-off requests.

segments.title: Motion Carries
segments.takeaway: The committee unanimously approved the motion, directing administration to report back with options for horse-drawn carriage business licensing and a framework for unique business requests.
